    50:           -A OUTPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    51:           -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT

    53:           -A INPUT -p udp -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT

    44:         - update_git

    46:         - name: Update project using git

    89:

    94:         - name: Ensure the project directory is present
    95:           ansible.builtin.file:
    96:             dest: "{{ project_path | quote }}"

    99:

   131:             url: "{{ scm_url | quote }}"
   132:             dest: "{{ project_path | quote }}/.archive/"
   133:             url_username: "{{ scm_username | default(omit) }}"

   137:           register: get_archive

   143:             force: "{{ scm_clean }}"
   144:           when: get_archive.changed or scm_clean

   147:         - name: Find previous archives
   148:           ansible.builtin.find:

   171:         - update_svn
   172:         - update_insights
   173:         - update_archive
   174:

   176:   gather_facts: false
   177:   connection: local
   178:   name: Perform project signature/checksum verification
   179:   tasks:
   180:     - name: Verify project content using GPG signature
   181:       verify_project:

   183:         validation_type: gpg

   185:       tags:

   187: 
   188:     - name: Verify project content against checksum manifest

   193:         - validation_checksum_manifest

   201:     # additional_galaxy_env contains environment variables are used for installing roles and collections and will take precedence over items in galaxy_task_env
   202:     additional_galaxy_env:

   204:       ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH: "{{ projects_root }}/.__awx_cache/{{ local_path }}/stage/requirements_collections"

   223: 
   224:     - block:

   233:                 - "{{ project_path | quote }}/roles/requirements.yml"
   234:                 - "{{ project_path | quote }}/roles/requirements.yaml"
   235:               skip: True
   236:           changed_when: "'was installed successfully' in galaxy_result.stdout"
   237:           when:
   238:             - roles_enabled | bool
   239:             - req_file | length > 0
   240:           tags:
   241:             - install_roles
   242: 
   243:         - name: Fetch galaxy collections from collections/requirements.(yml/yaml)

   247:           vars:
   248:             req_file: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.first_found', req_candidates, skip=True) }}"
   249:             req_candidates:

    35:   community.docker.docker_container:
    36:     name: "{{ minecraft_game_container_name }}"

    39:     volumes:
    40:       - "{{ minecraft_game_data_dir }}:/data"
    41:     ports:
    42:       # Java Edition is TCP-only; there is no UDP counterpart to publish. This is the
    43:       # single port to forward on the router.
    44:       - "{{ minecraft_game_port }}:25565/tcp"

    46:       # console with full server authority behind one password, so publishing it on

    54:       LEVEL: "{{ minecraft_game_level }}"

    58:       GID: "{{ minecraft_game_gid }}"
    59:       MEMORY: "{{ minecraft_game_memory }}"
    60:       GAMEMODE: "survival"

    62:       MAX_PLAYERS: "20"
    63:       MOTD: "California | Java | Survival"

    66:       ONLINE_MODE: "true"
    67:       WHITELIST: "{{ minecraft_game_whitelist | join(',') }}"

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Real sshd on an alternate port, UGOS (UGREEN NAS) flavor.
     3: #
     4: # The Ubuntu hosts get their alternate port from sshd_alt_port by extending the stock
     5: # sshd's listen config. That approach is closed on UGOS: the vendor owns sshd_config
     6: # (global ForceCommand wrapper, admin-account passthrough — see rustd_backup_nas's
     7: # README for the field story), and its SFTP subsystem serves a chrooted share view
     8: # (/docker, /home, /storage) instead of the real filesystem. Shell exec passes through
     9: # the wrapper fine, so the rustd.xyz panel's command features (wipes, snapshots) work —
    10: # but every SFTP read against a real path fails ("Operation unsupported"), which is what
    11: # broke the panel's moderator roster, snapshot listing, blueprint scan and map fetch on
    12: # NAS-hosted servers (rustd.xyz#456).
    13: #
    14: # So instead of extending the vendor sshd, this runs a SECOND stock sshd instance with
    15: # its own clean config on the same port number sshd_alt_port uses everywhere else:
    16: #
    17: #   :22   -> vendor sshd, untouched (UGOS UI, wrapper, and whatever the vendor patches)
    18: #   :2222 -> stock OpenSSH: key-only auth, one allowed user, normal internal-sftp
    19: #
    20: # Same account, same groups, same filesystem as the wrapper shell — so pointing the
    21: # panel's credential at :2222 changes nothing about exec behaviour and simply makes
    22: # SFTP see the real filesystem. It also future-proofs the NAS against the Tailscale SSH
    23: # badge ever being enabled here (the exact port-22 interception sshd_alt_port exists for).
    24: #
    25: # The vendor config is never read or written; a firmware update that stomps
    26: # /etc/systemd/system or /etc/ssh/sshd_config_alt is repaired by re-running this role.
    27: 
    28: - name: Install the alternate sshd config
    29:   become: true
    30:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    31:     dest: /etc/ssh/sshd_config_alt
    32:     content: |
    33:       # Managed by ansible (sshd_alt_port_ugos). See the role for why this exists.
    34:       Port {{ sshd_alt_port_ugos_number }}
    35:       PidFile /run/sshd-alt.pid
    36:       PermitRootLogin no
    37:       PasswordAuthentication no
    38:       KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
    39:       UsePAM yes
    40:       AllowUsers {{ sshd_alt_port_ugos_allow_users }}
    41:       X11Forwarding no
    42:       Subsystem sftp internal-sftp
    43:     owner: root
    44:     group: root
    45:     mode: "0644"
    46:     validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
    47:   notify: Restart ssh-alt
    48: 
    49: - name: Install the ssh-alt systemd unit
    50:   become: true
    51:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    52:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/ssh-alt.service
    53:     content: |
    54:       # Managed by ansible (sshd_alt_port_ugos). See the role for why this exists.
    55:       [Unit]
    56:       Description=OpenSSH on the alternate port (clean config, no UGOS wrapper)
    57:       After=network.target
    58: 
    59:       [Service]
    60:       ExecStartPre=/usr/sbin/sshd -t -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config_alt
    61:       ExecStart=/usr/sbin/sshd -D -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config_alt
    62:       ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
    63:       KillMode=process
    64:       Restart=on-failure
    65: 
    66:       [Install]
    67:       WantedBy=multi-user.target
    68:     owner: root
    69:     group: root
    70:     mode: "0644"
    71:   notify: Restart ssh-alt
    72: 
    73: - name: Enable and start ssh-alt
    74:   become: true
    75:   ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
    76:     name: ssh-alt
    77:     enabled: true
    78:     state: started
    79:     daemon_reload: true

review_question: Would an average-task-size cutoff be a useful additional signal that this artifact needs decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Probe by BARE package name (no version suffix). apt-cache policy only accepts a
     3: # package name (pkg=version is apt-get syntax), and yum list with a version-pinned
     4: # spec is fragile against the repo's dist tag (e.g. -1.el7). The intent here is
     5: # simply "can this package be obtained from a repo or is it already installed"
     6: # before we remove the old packages, so the name is sufficient.
     7: - name: Check Package Availability (RedHat)  # noqa: command-instead-of-module
     8:   shell: |
     9:     yum list available {{ item }} 2>/dev/null || yum list installed {{ item }} 2>/dev/null
    10:   register: package_availability_check_redhat
    11:   changed_when: false
    12:   failed_when: false
    13:   check_mode: false
    14:   loop: "{{ validate_packages }}"
    15:   when:
    16:     - ansible_os_family == "RedHat"
    17:     - installation_method == "package"
    18:   tags:
    19:     - package
    20:     - cp_package
    21:     - validate_package_availability
    22: 
    23: - name: Check Package Availability (Debian)
    24:   shell: |
    25:     apt-cache policy {{ item }} 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'Candidate:' | grep -v 'Candidate: (none)'
    26:   register: package_availability_check_debian
    27:   changed_when: false
    28:   failed_when: false
    29:   check_mode: false
    30:   loop: "{{ validate_packages }}"
    31:   when:
    32:     - ansible_os_family == "Debian"
    33:     - installation_method == "package"
    34:   tags:
    35:     - package
    36:     - cp_package
    37:     - validate_package_availability
    38: 
    39: # Fail with an explicit list of the missing packages so support does not have to
    40: # parse raw yum/apt output to find out what is unavailable.
    41: - name: Fail if Any Package is Unavailable
    42:   fail:
    43:     msg: >-
    44:       Package(s) not available in any repo or installed:
    45:       {{ unavailable_packages | join(', ') }}. Aborting before removing old
    46:       packages. Check repo config and Confluent version ({{ confluent_package_version }}).
    47:   vars:
    48:     unavailable_packages: >-
    49:       {{ ((package_availability_check_redhat.results | default([]))
    50:           + (package_availability_check_debian.results | default([])))
    51:          | selectattr('rc', 'defined')
    52:          | selectattr('rc', 'ne', 0)
    53:          | map(attribute='item')
    54:          | list }}
    55:   when:
    56:     - installation_method == "package"
    57:     - unavailable_packages | length > 0
    58:   tags:
    59:     - package
    60:     - cp_package
    61:     - validate_package_availability

     5: # Taskfile wrapping `kubectl kopiur` for day-2 Kopiur operations. Assumes
     6: # Fluxtomization, HelmRelease, PVC, and SnapshotPolicy all share the app's
     7: # name (e.g. plex), and each application backs up exactly one PVC. The
     8: # kubectl-kopiur plugin replaces what used to be hand-rolled Job/template

    11: tasks:
    12:   state-*:
    13:     desc: Suspend or resume the shared r2 ClusterRepository (pauses every app's backups)
    14:     cmds:
    15:       - kubectl kopiur {{.STATE}} cluster-repository r2
    16:     vars:
    17:       STATE: "{{index .MATCH 0}}"
    18:     preconditions:
    19:       - '[[ "{{.STATE}}" == "suspend" || "{{.STATE}}" == "resume" ]]'
    20:       - which kubectl kubectl-kopiur
    21: 
    22:   snapshot:
    23:     desc: Snapshot an app now [NS=default] [APP=required]
    24:     cmds:
    25:       - kubectl kopiur snapshot now --policy {{.APP}} -n {{.NS}} --wait
    26:     vars:
    27:       NS: '{{.NS | default "default"}}'
    28:     requires:
    29:       vars: [APP]
    30:     preconditions:
    31:       - kubectl --namespace {{.NS}} get snapshotpolicy {{.APP}}
    32:       - which kubectl kubectl-kopiur

    34:   restore:

    37:       # Suspend

    39:       - flux --namespace {{.NS}} suspend helmrelease {{.APP}}
    40:       - kubectl --namespace {{.NS}} scale {{.CONTROLLER}}/{{.APP}} --replicas 0
    41:       - kubectl --namespace {{.NS}} wait pod --for=delete --selector="app.kubernetes.io/name={{.APP}}" --timeout=5m

    44:         kubectl kopiur restore --from-policy {{.APP}}

     3: # shared connection (URL + per-tier tokens) to OpenBao secret/ai/mcp/vikunja.

     5: # Mirrors ansible-splunk roles/splunk_docker/tasks/manage_one_user.yml:
     6: #   * mint only when absent (idempotent — Vikunja returns the key exactly once)
     7: #   * sibling-preserving KV-v2 read-modify-write

    10: # The converge enables it with -e '{"vikunja_token_publish_openbao": true}';
    11: # BAO_ADDR/BAO_TOKEN must be in the CONTROLLER environment.
    12: #
    13: # Permissions are built from the LIVE GET /api/v1/routes response, never
    14: # hardcoded: Vikunja's PermissionsAreValid rejects any group/action not in the
    15: # current route set, and the route-group keys are derived from URL paths (so
    16: # they shift across versions). Building from the running instance keeps the
    17: # minted permissions valid by construction.
    18: 
    19: - name: Assert OpenBao write credentials are present
    20:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    21:     that:
    22:       - vikunja_token_openbao_addr | length > 0

     3: # policy grants <ssh_mount>/roles/<name> but nothing on sys/mounts or
     4: # ssh/config/ca, so each of these 403s under a reconcile-mode run. Note the
     5: # reconcile login assigns its token to openbao_bootstrap_token, so
     6: # `openbao_bootstrap_token is defined` no longer means "operator token" and
     7: # cannot gate a privileged task on its own.
     8: #
     9: # The CA probe is gated too, not just the write: it runs under
    10: # failed_when: false, and a DENIED read returns rc != 0 exactly like an absent
    11: # CA — which then triggers the privileged key generation that cannot succeed.
    12: #
    13: # The SSH signing ROLES below stay ungated: they are in the reconcile policy by
    14: # design, and skipping them would silently stop reconciling them.
    15: - name: Enable the SSH secrets engine
    16:   ansible.builtin.command:
    17:     cmd: "bao secrets enable -path={{ openbao_ssh_mount }} ssh"
    18:   environment:
    19:     BAO_ADDR: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}"
    20:     BAO_TOKEN: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"
    21:   no_log: true
    22:   changed_when: true
    23:   when:
    24:     - not (openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false))
    25:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
    26:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
    27:     - (openbao_ssh_mount ~ '/') not in (openbao_mounts_raw.stdout | from_json).keys()
    28: 
    29: # Write-once: the CA keypair is generated INSIDE OpenBao on first configuration
    30: # and never exported; a routine converge with a CA already configured leaves it
    31: # untouched (rotation is a deliberate operator action via the multi-issuer API).

    33:   ansible.builtin.command:
    34:     cmd: "bao read -format=json {{ openbao_ssh_mount }}/config/ca"

    36:     BAO_ADDR: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}"
    37:     BAO_TOKEN: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"

    39:   no_log: true
    40:   changed_when: false
    41:   failed_when: false
    42:   when:
    43:     - not (openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false))
    44:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
    45:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool

    53:     body_format: json

    55:     # converge fails loudly here — do NOT silently fall back; see defaults.
    56:     body: >-
    57:       {{ {'generate_signing_key': true}
    58:          | combine({'key_type': openbao_ssh_ca_key_type} if openbao_ssh_ca_key_type | length > 0 else {}) }}
    59:     status_code:
    60:       - 200
    61:       - 204
    62:   no_log: true
    63:   changed_when: true

    67:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
    68:     - (openbao_ssh_ca_check.rc | default(1)) != 0
    69: 
    70: # Surface the CA public key + fingerprint ONCE, in this verified bootstrap
    71: # session — this is the trusted ceremony the ssh_ca_trust role's pinned
    72: # fingerprint comes from (committed as reviewable IaC data, human-reviewed
    73: # before any trust rollout). Public material only; safe to log.
    74: - name: Read the SSH CA public key
    75:   ansible.builtin.command:
    76:     cmd: "bao read -field=public_key {{ openbao_ssh_mount }}/config/ca"
    77:   environment:
    78:     BAO_ADDR: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}"
    79:     BAO_TOKEN: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"
    80:   register: openbao_ssh_ca_public_key
    81:   changed_when: false
    82:   when:
    83:     - not (openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false))
    84:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
    85:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
    86: 
    87: - name: Show the SSH CA public key fingerprint (pin this in ssh_ca_trust)
    88:   ansible.builtin.shell:
    89:     cmd: >-
    90:       set -o pipefail;
    91:       printf '%s\n' "{{ openbao_ssh_ca_public_key.stdout }}"
    92:       | ssh-keygen -l -f /dev/stdin
    93:     executable: /bin/bash
    94:   register: openbao_ssh_ca_fingerprint
    95:   changed_when: false
    96:   when:
    97:     - not (openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false))
    98:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
    99:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
   100: 
   101: - name: Report the SSH CA fingerprint
   102:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   103:     msg: "SSH CA fingerprint (pin in ansible-proxmox ssh_ca_trust): {{ openbao_ssh_ca_fingerprint.stdout }}"
   104:   when:
   105:     - not (openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false))
   106:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   107:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
   108: 
   109: - name: Warn when no source-address restriction is configured for SSH certs
   110:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   111:     msg: >-
   112:       OPENBAO_SSH_SOURCE_CIDRS is unset — SSH certificates will be valid from
   113:       ANY source address. Documented residual: compensated by the guest
   114:       firewall default-deny layer. Set the env var (Doppler) to add the
   115:       source-address critical option.
   116:   when:
   117:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   118:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
   119:     - openbao_ssh_source_address_cidrs | length == 0
   120: 
   121: - name: Check which SSH signing roles already exist
   122:   ansible.builtin.command:
   123:     cmd: "bao read -format=json {{ openbao_ssh_mount }}/roles/{{ item.name }}"
   124:   environment:
   125:     BAO_ADDR: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}"
   126:     BAO_TOKEN: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"
   127:   loop: "{{ openbao_ssh_roles }}"
   128:   loop_control:
   129:     label: "{{ item.name }}"
   130:   register: openbao_ssh_role_checks
   131:   no_log: true
   132:   changed_when: false
   133:   failed_when: false
   134:   when:
   135:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   136:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
   137: 
   138: # Explicit principals only — never allowed_users="*" (documented upstream
   139: # wildcard bug, and a wildcard would defeat the per-principal-class design).
   140: # ttl == max_ttl: a sign request may shorten a cert's life, never extend it.
   141: - name: Reconcile the SSH signing roles
   142:   ansible.builtin.uri:
   143:     url: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}/v1/{{ openbao_ssh_mount }}/roles/{{ item.0.name }}"
   144:     method: POST
   145:     headers:
   146:       X-Vault-Token: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"
   147:     body_format: json
   148:     body: >-
   149:       {{ {
   150:            'key_type': 'ca',
   151:            'allow_user_certificates': true,
   152:            'allowed_users': item.0.principal,
   153:            'default_user': item.0.principal,
   154:            'ttl': item.0.ttl,
   155:            'max_ttl': item.0.ttl,
   156:            'allowed_extensions': item.0.extensions.keys() | join(','),
   157:            'default_extensions': item.0.extensions,
   158:            'algorithm_signer': 'default'
   159:          }
   160:          | combine({'default_critical_options': {'source-address': openbao_ssh_source_address_cidrs}}
   161:                    if openbao_ssh_source_address_cidrs | length > 0 else {}) }}
   162:     status_code:
   163:       - 200
   164:       - 204
   165:   loop: >-
   166:     {{ openbao_ssh_roles
   167:        | zip(openbao_ssh_role_checks.results | default([])) | list }}
   168:   loop_control:
   169:     label: "{{ item.0.name }}"
   170:   no_log: true
   171:   changed_when: >-
   172:     (item.1.rc | default(1)) != 0
   173:     or (item.1.stdout | from_json).data.max_ttl != item.0.ttl
   174:   when:
   175:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   176:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
   177: 
   178: # --- Fail-closed guard: no AI capability leaf for the control plane / kernel --
   179: # The base read-/write- leaves are rendered blindly from openbao_ai_domains +
   180: # openbao_ai_readonly_extra_subtrees. A typo or malicious entry naming the IaC
   181: # kernel or a control-plane mount (infra / sys / auth) would mint a leaf granting
   182: # it, and every rollup composed of leaves would inherit it — the one way the
   183: # enumerated-allowlist proof could be subverted. Refuse before rendering anything.
   184: - name: Assert no AI capability subtree names a forbidden control-plane path
   185:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   186:     that:
   187:       - (openbao_ai_domains + openbao_ai_readonly_extra_subtrees)
   188:         | map('lower') | select('in', openbao_ai_forbidden_subtrees) | list | length == 0
   189:     fail_msg: >-
   190:       An AI capability subtree names a forbidden control-plane/kernel path
   191:       ({{ openbao_ai_forbidden_subtrees | join(', ') }}). Refusing to render base
   192:       read-/write- leaves — this would grant the IaC kernel or the policy/auth
   193:       control plane and break the self-escalation invariant.
   194:     success_msg: "AI capability subtrees are all outside the control plane/kernel."
   195:   when: openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   196: 
   197: # Companion guard for the ssh-sign leaves: they are the one DELIBERATE grant
   198: # class outside secret/, allowlisted to exactly <ssh mount>/sign/<enumerated
   199: # role>. Refuse if the mount collides with a control-plane path or a sign leaf
   200: # names a role outside the enumerated openbao_ssh_roles table.
   201: - name: Assert ssh-sign leaves stay inside the enumerated SSH CA sign allowlist
   202:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   203:     that:
   204:       - openbao_ssh_mount not in (openbao_ai_forbidden_subtrees + [openbao_kv_mount])
   205:       - >-
   206:         openbao_ssh_sign_policies | map(attribute='ssh_role')
   207:         | reject('in', openbao_ssh_roles | map(attribute='name') | list)
   208:         | list | length == 0
   209:     fail_msg: >-
   210:       An ssh-sign policy targets a mount or role outside the enumerated SSH CA
   211:       allowlist ({{ openbao_ssh_mount }}/sign/<{{ openbao_ssh_roles | map(attribute='name') | join('|') }}>).
   212:       Refusing to render.
   213:     success_msg: "ssh-sign leaves are confined to the enumerated SSH CA sign endpoints."
   214:   when:
   215:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   216:     - openbao_ssh_engine_enabled | bool
   217: 
   218: # --- RBAC policies (write-if-missing-or-changed) ----------------------------
   219: # Rendered on the TARGET: `bao policy write` below executes there and reads
   220: # the file from its local filesystem (a controller-side render is unreachable
   221: # from the target). Policy HCL is non-secret — it comes from the committed
   222: # templates. Rendered into openbao_config_dir (/etc/openbao, 0750 root:openbao)
   223: # rather than world-writable /tmp, so the write is not exposed to symlink races
   224: # or other local users on the host.

name: roles/technitium_dns/tasks/main/forwarders_and_zones.yml
review_question: Would an average-task-size cutoff be a useful additional signal that this artifact needs decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Forward every non-authoritative query (the apex + public names) over encrypted
     3: # DoH to the configured upstreams, with EDNS Client Subnet disabled so the
     4: # client subnet is never sent to upstream resolvers. DNSSEC validation stays on.
     5: # This is a server-level setting, so it runs on EVERY node: each instance is a
     6: # full resolver — authoritative/secondary for the subdomain, forward the rest.
     7: - name: Configure upstream forwarders (encrypted DoH)
     8:   delegate_to: localhost
     9:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    10:     url: "{{ technitium_dns_api_url }}/api/settings/set?token={{ technitium_dns_api_token }}"
    11:     method: POST
    12:     body_format: form-urlencoded
    13:     body:
    14:       forwarders: "{{ technitium_dns_forwarders | join(',') }}"
    15:       forwarderProtocol: "{{ technitium_dns_forwarder_protocol }}"
    16:       eDnsClientSubnet: "{{ technitium_dns_edns_client_subnet | string | lower }}"
    17:       dnssecValidation: "true"
    18:     return_content: true
    19:     timeout: "{{ technitium_dns_api_timeout }}"
    20:   register: technitium_dns_forwarders_result
    21:   changed_when: technitium_dns_forwarders_result.json.status == "ok"
    22:   when: technitium_dns_apply | bool
    23:   no_log: true
    24: 
    25: # NOTE: this role deliberately does NOT delete the apex zone (jacobpevans.com).
    26: # A prior "remove stale apex Primary zone" task deleted the WHOLE apex zone
    27: # whenever it existed, on the false premise that (a) a pre-existing apex zone
    28: # was leftover cruft and (b) the subdomain-zone create would 400 while it
    29: # existed. Both are wrong: the apex Route53-mirrored zone can hold live records
    30: # (the pve node A records), and a parent Primary + child Primary coexist fine
    31: # (this server runs both the apex zone and its child subdomain zone
    32: # simultaneously
    33: # today). Deleting the apex was purely destructive and once caused a live
    34: # outage. Non-authoritative apex names already FORWARD to the upstream
    35: # resolvers (configured above) whether or not any apex zone exists locally, so
    36: # there is nothing to "clean up" here.
    37: #
    38: # CANONICAL ZONE FOR A GUEST HOSTNAME: technitium_dns_zone (the subdomain)
    39: # only. The per-guest A-record builder above writes exclusively into that
    40: # zone — it has never written per-guest records into the apex zone. A guest
    41: # created before this role became subdomain-only kept whatever apex-zone
    42: # record it already had (frozen there, unmaintained, per the NOTE above);
    43: # every guest created since has NO apex-zone record, by design. So an
    44: # apex-zone NXDOMAIN for a guest hostname means only "this guest postdates
    45: # the migration to a subdomain-only zone" — it is NOT a liveness signal and
    46: # must never be read as "this guest is down". Any health check, monitor, or
    47: # runbook resolving a GUEST hostname must query technitium_dns_zone, never
    48: # the apex.
    49: #
    50: # EXCEPTION — the cluster nodes themselves are the opposite: they have NO
    51: # record in the subdomain zone at all. Their only A-records are the apex
    52: # round-robin set this role writes below (technitium_dns_proxmox_endpoint_a_records
    53: # / the Traefik apex fallback), which is a separate write path from the
    54: # per-guest builder above. For a cluster node name, the apex is the only
    55: # zone that was ever authoritative — an apex-zone NXDOMAIN there DOES mean
    56: # the node is missing from that record set, and the subdomain zone has
    57: # nothing to fall back to.
    58: #
    59: # THIRD CASE — a Traefik-fronted SERVICE name's apex record is not merely
    60: # stale, it is actively wrong: it still holds the direct pre-migration
    61: # backend address instead of the Traefik VIP its subdomain alias correctly
    62: # points at, and the old backend no longer terminates TLS there. The apex
    63: # form of the name therefore resolves, then hangs until timeout — it does
    64: # not NXDOMAIN, so it reads as "service is down" while both the service and
    65: # the name are otherwise healthy. Same root cause as the guest case above
    66: # (this role has never written into the apex zone since narrowing to the
    67: # subdomain), different symptom because these names predate the migration
    68: # with a real value instead of no value at all.
    69: - name: Create authoritative subdomain DNS zone (primary)
    70:   delegate_to: localhost
    71:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    72:     url: "{{ technitium_dns_api_url }}/api/zones/create?token={{ technitium_dns_api_token }}"
    73:     method: POST
    74:     body_format: form-urlencoded
    75:     body:
    76:       zone: "{{ technitium_dns_zone }}"
    77:       type: "{{ technitium_dns_zone_type }}"
    78:     return_content: true
    79:     timeout: "{{ technitium_dns_api_timeout }}"
    80:     status_code: [200, 400]
    81:   register: technitium_dns_zone_create
    82:   changed_when: technitium_dns_zone_create.json.status == "ok"
    83:   failed_when:
    84:     - technitium_dns_zone_create.json.status | default('') != "ok"
    85:     - "'already exists' not in (technitium_dns_zone_create.json.errorMessage | default(''))"
    86:   when:
    87:     - technitium_dns_role == 'primary'
    88:     - technitium_dns_apply | bool
    89:     - technitium_dns_zone not in technitium_dns_existing_zones
    90:   no_log: true
    91: 
    92: # Secondaries replicate the zone from the primary via native AXFR/IXFR zone
    93: # transfer; they create a Secondary zone (master = primary) and skip all record
    94: # writes below. Only functions once the primary + secondary LXCs exist.
    95: - name: Create Secondary DNS zone (secondary)
    96:   delegate_to: localhost
    97:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    98:     url: "{{ technitium_dns_api_url }}/api/zones/create?token={{ technitium_dns_api_token }}"
    99:     method: POST
   100:     body_format: form-urlencoded
   101:     body:
   102:       zone: "{{ technitium_dns_zone }}"
   103:       type: "Secondary"
   104:       primaryNameServerAddresses: "{{ technitium_dns_primary_ip }}"
   105:       zoneTransferProtocol: "{{ technitium_dns_zone_transfer_protocol }}"
   106:     return_content: true
   107:     timeout: "{{ technitium_dns_api_timeout }}"
   108:     status_code: [200, 400]
   109:   register: technitium_dns_secondary_zone_create
   110:   changed_when: technitium_dns_secondary_zone_create.json.status == "ok"
   111:   when:
   112:     - technitium_dns_role == 'secondary'
   113:     - technitium_dns_apply | bool
   114:     - technitium_dns_zone not in technitium_dns_existing_zones
   115:   no_log: true

     3: #
     4:

     6: - wait_for: timeout=5
     7: 
     8: ####################
     9: # Set up variables #
    10: ####################
    11: 
    12: - name: Set admin_user ID
    13:   set_fact: admin_user_id="{{ 9999999999999999999999 | random | to_uuid }}"
    14: 
    15: #####################
    16: # Disable authtoken #
    17: #####################
    18: 
    19: - name: Find ID of authtoken module, if enabled
    20:   uri:
    21:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/_/proxy/tenants/{{ tenant }}/interfaces/authtoken"
    22:     headers:
    23:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "supertenant"

    25:       Accept: "application/json, text/plain"

    27: 
    28: - name: Disable authtoken without dependency checking
    29:   uri:
    30:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/_/proxy/tenants/{{ tenant }}/install?depCheck=false"
    31:     method: POST
    32:     body_format: json
    33:     headers:
    34:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "supertenant"
    35:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ supertenant_token | default('') }}"
    36:       Accept: "application/json, text/plain"

    39:   when: authtoken_module.json.0 is defined
    40: 
    41: ########################

    43: ########################
    44: 
    45: - name: Bootstrap admin user
    46:   block:
    47:     - name: Check for user record
    48:       uri:
    49:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/users?query=username%3d%3d{{ admin_user.username }}"
    50:         headers:
    51:           Accept: "application/json, text/plain"
    52:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    53:       register: check_user
    54:     - name: Get user ID if user already exists
    55:       set_fact:
    56:         admin_user_id: "{{ check_user.json.users.0.id }}"
    57:       when: check_user.json.totalRecords > 0
    58:     - name: Create user record
    59:       uri:
    60:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/users"
    61:         method: POST
    62:         body_format: json
    63:         headers:
    64:           Accept: "application/json, text/plain"
    65:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    66:         body: |
    67:           {
    68:             "id": "{{ admin_user_id }}",

    77:           }
    78:         status_code: 201
    79:       register: create_user
    80:       changed_when: create_user.status == 201
    81:       when: check_user.json.totalRecords == 0
    82:     - name: Check for login record
    83:       uri:
    84:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/authn/credentials-existence?userId={{ admin_user_id }}"
    85:         headers:
    86:           Accept: "application/json, text/plain"
    87:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    88:       register: check_login
    89:     - name: Create login record
    90:       uri:
    91:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/authn/credentials"
    92:         method: POST
    93:         body_format: json
    94:         headers:
    95:           Accept: "application/json, text/plain"
    96:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    97:         body: |
    98:           {
    99:             "userId": "{{ admin_user_id }}",
   100:             "password": "{{ admin_user.password }}"
   101:           }
   102:         status_code: 201
   103:       register: create_login
   104:       changed_when: create_login.status == 201
   105:       when: check_login.json.credentialsExist == false
   106:     - name: Check for permissions record
   107:       uri:
   108:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/perms/users?query=userId%3d%3d{{ admin_user_id }}"
   109:         headers:
   110:           Accept: "application/json, text/plain"
   111:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
   112:       register: check_perms
   113:     - name: Create permissions record

   115:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/perms/users"
   116:         method: POST

   118:         headers:

   120:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
   121:         body: |
   122:           {
   123:             "userId": "{{ admin_user_id }}",

   125:           {% if perms_users_assign|default(false) %}

   130:               "perms.all"
   131:             ]
   132:           }
   133:         status_code: 201
   134:       register: create_login
   135:       changed_when: create_login.status == 201
   136:       when: check_perms.json.totalRecords == 0
   137:     - name: Check for service-points-users interface
   138:       uri:
   139:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/_/proxy/tenants/{{ tenant }}/interfaces/service-points-users"
   140:         headers:
   141:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "supertenant"
   142:           X-Okapi-Token: "{{ supertenant_token | default('') }}"
   143:           Accept: "application/json, text/plain"
   144:       register: check_sp_users_int
   145:     - name: Check for service-points-users record
   146:       uri:
   147:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/service-points-users?query=userId%3d%3d{{ admin_user_id }}"
   148:         headers:
   149:           Accept: "application/json, text/plain"
   150:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
   151:       register: check_sp_user
   152:       when: check_sp_users_int.json|default([])|length > 0
   153:     - name: Get service points
   154:       uri:
   155:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/service-points"
   156:         headers:
   157:           Accept: application/json
   158:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
   159:       register: service_points
   160:       when: check_sp_users_int.json|default([])|length > 0 and check_sp_user.json.totalRecords == 0
   161:     - name: Set list of service point ids
   162:       set_fact: service_points_ids={{ '\"' + service_points|json_query('json.servicepoints[*].id')|join('\", \"') + '\"' }}
   163:       when: check_sp_users_int.json|default([])|length > 0 and check_sp_user.json.totalRecords == 0
   164:     # This can safely fail
   165:     - name: Create service points user
   166:       uri:
   167:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/service-points-users"
   168:         method: POST
   169:         body_format: json
   170:         headers:
   171:           Accept: application/json
   172:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
   173:         status_code: 201,422
   174:         body: >-
   175:           {
   176:           "userId": "{{ admin_user_id }}",
   177:           "servicePointsIds": [ {{ service_points_ids }} ],
   178:           "defaultServicePointId": "{{ service_points|json_query('json.servicepoints[*].id')|first }}"
   179:           }
   180:       register: create_sp_user
   181:       changed_when: create_sp_user.status == 201
   182:       when: check_sp_users_int.json|default([])|length > 0 and check_sp_user.json.totalRecords == 0
   183:       ignore_errors: yes
   184:   always:
   185:     ####################
   186:     # Enable authtoken #
   187:     ####################
   188:     - name: Build authtoken_enable list
   189:       set_fact:
   190:         authtoken_enable: "{{ authtoken_enable|default([]) + [ { 'id': item.id, 'action': 'enable' } ] }}"
   191:       when: authtoken_module.json.0 is defined
   192:       with_items: "{{ authtoken_disable.json|reverse|list }}"
   193: 
   194:     - name: Enable authtoken
   195:       uri:
   196:         url: "{{ okapi_url }}/_/proxy/tenants/{{ tenant }}/install?depCheck=false"
   197:         method: POST
   198:         body_format: json
   199:         headers:
   200:           X-Okapi-Tenant: "supertenant"
   201:           X-Okapi-Token: "{{ supertenant_token | default('') }}"
   202:           Accept: "application/json, text/plain"
   203:         body: "{{ authtoken_enable }}"

   205:       when: authtoken_module.json.0 is defined

    78:         }

    82:           Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -like '{{ item.match }}' }

   152:         }

source_context:
1: # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025 Slavi Pantaleev
     2: #
     3: # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
     4: 
     5: ---
     6: 
     7: # ansible-role-docker creates the Docker daemon options file (`/etc/docker/daemon.json`) when options are set
     8: # via `mash_playbook_docker_installation_daemon_options` (which influences the `docker_daemon_options` variable of the role).
     9: # See: https://github.com/geerlingguy/ansible-role-docker/blob/acade8d01f11bcd5efecba6d8211138d7567ce4b/tasks/main.yml#L53-L66
    10: #
    11: # However, it doesn't delete the file when the options list is empty.
    12: #
    13: # This means that people who previously force-disabled IPv6 (and injected `{'ipv6': false}` options, etc)
    14: # or had some other custom options had that file created for them.
    15: # Later, when they stopped setting these options, they were stuck with the configuration file that still retained them.
    16: #
    17: # Here, we make the file go away of no options are set.
    18: # Ideally, this task would be part of the `ansible-role-docker` role, but it's not (yet).
    19: # See: https://github.com/geerlingguy/ansible-role-docker/pull/498
    20: - name: Ensure the Docker daemon options file is deleted when no longer needed
    21:   when: mash_playbook_docker_installation_daemon_options.keys() | length == 0
    22:   ansible.builtin.file:
    23:     path: "{{ mash_playbook_docker_installation_daemon_options_file_path }}"
    24:     state: absent
    25:   notify: restart docker

     9:         combine(dict(workload_priority_production_namespaces |

    12:         combine(dict(workload_priority_environment_namespaces |
    13:                      zip(['platform-preproduction'] *
    14:                          (workload_priority_environment_namespaces | length)))) |
    15:         combine(dict(workload_priority_review_namespaces |
    16:                      zip(['platform-preproduction'] *
    17:                          (workload_priority_review_namespaces | length))))
    18:       }}
    19: 
    20: - name: Workload priority | Label classified namespaces
    21:   kubernetes.core.k8s:
    22:     state: present
    23:     definition:
    24:       apiVersion: v1
    25:       kind: Namespace
    26:       metadata:
    27:         name: '{{ item.key }}'
    28:         labels:
    29:           platform.example.com/environment-tier: >-
    30:             {{
    31:               'platform' if item.value == 'platform-platform-critical'
    32:               else 'production' if item.value == 'platform-production'
    33:               else 'environment' if item.value == 'platform-preproduction'
    34:               else 'review'
    35:             }}
    36:           platform.example.com/priority-class: '{{ item.value }}'
    37:   loop: '{{ _workload_priority_namespace_map | dict2items }}'
    38:   loop_control:
    39:     label: '{{ item.key }} -> {{ item.value }}'
    40: 
    41: - name: Workload priority | Discover Deployments
    42:   kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
    43:     api_version: apps/v1
    44:     kind: Deployment
    45:   register: _workload_priority_deployments
    46: 
    47: - name: Workload priority | Discover StatefulSets
    48:   kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
    49:     api_version: apps/v1
    50:     kind: StatefulSet
    51:   register: _workload_priority_statefulsets
    52: 
    53: - name: Workload priority | Discover DaemonSets
    54:   kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
    55:     api_version: apps/v1
    56:     kind: DaemonSet
    57:   register: _workload_priority_daemonsets
    58: 
    59: - name: Workload priority | Build controller inventory
    60:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    61:     _workload_priority_controllers: >-
    62:       {{
    63:         (_workload_priority_deployments.resources | default([])) +
    64:         (_workload_priority_statefulsets.resources | default([])) +
    65:         (_workload_priority_daemonsets.resources | default([]))
    66:       }}
    67: 
    68: - name: Workload priority | Apply and gate each controller serially
    69:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: apply-controller.yml
    70:   loop: '{{ _workload_priority_controllers }}'
    71:   loop_control:
    72:     label: >-
    73:       {{ item.metadata.namespace }}/{{ item.kind }}/{{ item.metadata.name }}
    74:   when:
    75:     - item.metadata.namespace in _workload_priority_namespace_map
    76:     - >-
    77:       (item.metadata.namespace ~ '/' ~ item.kind ~ '/' ~ item.metadata.name)
    78:       not in workload_priority_temporary_exclusions
    79:     # Never downgrade Kubernetes system classes or replace an intentional
    80:     # component-specific class (for example a CI manager or cache). This role
    81:     # only closes the unsafe "no priority" gap.
    82:     - (item.spec.template.spec.priorityClassName | default('') | length) == 0
    83: 
    84: - name: Workload priority | Verify no classified workload is left unprioritized
    85:   ansible.builtin.command:
    86:     argv:
    87:       - kubectl
    88:       - get
    89:       - deployment,statefulset,daemonset
    90:       - --all-namespaces
    91:       - --output=json
    92:   register: _workload_priority_verification
    93:   changed_when: false
    94: 
    95: - name: Workload priority | Resolve unprioritized controller keys
    96:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    97:     _workload_priority_unprioritized_keys: >-
    98:       {%- set missing = [] -%}
    99:       {%- for controller in
   100:             ((_workload_priority_verification.stdout | from_json)['items'] |
   101:              default([])) -%}
   102:       {%-   if controller.metadata.namespace in
   103:               (_workload_priority_namespace_map.keys() | list) and
   104:               not (controller.spec.template.spec.priorityClassName is defined) -%}
   105:       {%-     set _ = missing.append(
   106:                 controller.metadata.namespace ~ '/' ~ controller.kind ~ '/' ~
   107:                 controller.metadata.name) -%}
   108:       {%-   endif -%}
   109:       {%- endfor -%}
   110:       {{ missing }}
   111: 
   112: - name: Workload priority | Assert the reconciled service boundary
   113:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   114:     that:
   115:       - >-
   116:         (_workload_priority_unprioritized_keys |
   117:          difference(workload_priority_temporary_exclusions) | length) == 0
   118:     fail_msg: >-
   119:       At least one non-deferred classified workload controller has no
   120:       PriorityClass after reconciliation; refusing to declare the shared
   121:       worker pool safe. Missing={{ _workload_priority_unprioritized_keys }}
   122: 
   123: - name: Workload priority | Report explicitly deferred controllers
   124:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   125:     msg: >-
   126:       Priority reconciliation is temporarily deferred for
   127:       {{ _workload_priority_unprioritized_keys |
   128:          intersect(workload_priority_temporary_exclusions) }}. Run the final
   129:       audit with workload_priority_temporary_exclusions=[] after the active
   130:       operation completes.
   131:   when: >-
   132:     (_workload_priority_unprioritized_keys |
   133:      intersect(workload_priority_temporary_exclusions) | length) > 0

    51:     # Enable write operations to the OVN Northbound (matches `make testbed`).

    53: 
    54:     # Per-chassis Open_vSwitch visibility. The map keys are chassis system-ids
    55:     # (== node hostname) and the values are the OVSDB management address the node
    56:     # listens on (ptcp:6640:{{ internal_address }}, configured by the second play

    62: 
    63:     northwatch_config_dir: /etc/northwatch
    64:     northwatch_config_file: "{{ northwatch_config_dir }}/clusters.json"
    65:     northwatch_ovs_map_file: "{{ northwatch_config_dir }}/ovs-mgmt-addr.json"
    66: 
    67:     # Multi-cluster JSON config (--config-file / NORTHWATCH_CONFIG_FILE). Overrides
    68:     # the flat NB/SB env vars and carries the OpenStack enrichment credentials.
    69:     northwatch_clusters:
    70:       clusters:
    71:         - name: testbed
    72:           label: OSISM Testbed
    73:           ovn_nb_addr: "{{ northwatch_ovn_nb_addr }}"
    74:           ovn_sb_addr: "{{ northwatch_ovn_sb_addr }}"
    75:           enrichment:
    76:             type: openstack

    78:             os_username: "{{ northwatch_os_username }}"
    79:             os_password: "{{ northwatch_os_password }}"
    80:             os_project_name: "{{ northwatch_os_project_name }}"

    88:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    89:         name: northwatch
    90:         state: restarted
    91: 
    92:   tasks:
    93:     - name: Install the Northwatch package
    94:       become: true
    95:       ansible.builtin.apt:
    96:         deb: "{{ northwatch_deb_url }}"
    97:       register: result
    98:       until: result is succeeded
    99:       retries: 5

   103:     - name: Create the Northwatch configuration directory

   106:         path: "{{ northwatch_config_dir }}"
   107:         state: directory
   108:         mode: "0750"
   109:         owner: root
   110:         group: northwatch
   111: 
   112:     - name: Write the Northwatch multi-cluster configuration
   113:       become: true

   115:         content: "{{ northwatch_clusters | to_nice_json }}\n"
   116:         dest: "{{ northwatch_config_file }}"
   117:         mode: "0640"
   118:         owner: root
   119:         group: northwatch
   120:       notify: Restart northwatch
   121: 
   122:     - name: Write the Open_vSwitch management-address mapping
   123:       become: true
   124:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   125:         content: "{{ northwatch_ovs_map | to_nice_json }}\n"
   126:         dest: "{{ northwatch_ovs_map_file }}"
   127:         mode: "0640"
   128:         owner: root
   129:         group: northwatch
   130:       when: northwatch_ovs_enabled | bool
   131:       notify: Restart northwatch
   132: 
   133:     - name: Configure the Northwatch service environment
   134:       become: true
   135:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   136:         dest: /etc/default/northwatch
   137:         mode: "0640"
   138:         owner: root
   139:         group: northwatch
   140:         content: |
   141:           # Managed by environments/custom/playbook-northwatch.yml — do not edit by hand.
   142:           # Environment for northwatch.service (flags > env vars).
   143: 
   144:           # Multi-cluster JSON config: carries the OVN NB/SB addresses and the
   145:           # OpenStack enrichment credentials for the testbed cluster.
   146:           NORTHWATCH_CONFIG_FILE={{ northwatch_config_file }}
   147: 
   148:           # HTTP listen address for the dashboard/API (no built-in auth).
   149:           NORTHWATCH_LISTEN={{ northwatch_listen }}
   150: 
   151:           # Enable write operations to the OVN Northbound.
   152:           NORTHWATCH_WRITE_ENABLED={{ northwatch_write_enabled | bool | ternary('true', 'false') }}
   153: 
   154:           # SQLite history DB, persisted under the systemd StateDirectory.
   155:           NORTHWATCH_HISTORY_DB_PATH=/var/lib/northwatch/history.db
   156:           {% if northwatch_ovs_enabled | bool %}
   157:           # Per-chassis Open_vSwitch visibility (system-id -> OVSDB mgmt address).
   158:           NORTHWATCH_OVS_MGMT_ADDR_FILE={{ northwatch_ovs_map_file }}
   159:           {% endif %}
   160:       notify: Restart northwatch
   161: 
   162:     - name: Enable and start the Northwatch service
   163:       become: true
   164:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   165:         name: northwatch
   166:         enabled: true
   167:         state: started
   168: 
   169:     - name: Show how to reach the Northwatch dashboard
   170:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   171:         msg: >-
   172:           Northwatch {{ northwatch_version }} is running on the manager. Open
   173:           http://{{ internal_address }}{{ northwatch_listen }} over the VPN/SSH
   174:           tunnel (NB {{ northwatch_ovn_nb_addr }}).
   175: 
   176: # Configure the OVSDB managers (TCP listener on port 6640) on every node running
   177: # Open vSwitch (the openvswitch_db container), so Northwatch can pull per-chassis
   178: # OVS visibility. A listener is added on 127.0.0.1 and on the node's own internal
   179: # management address. Guarded by the presence of the openvswitch_db container and
   180: # made idempotent via a get-manager comparison. Skipped when OVS visibility is
   181: # disabled (northwatch_ovs_enabled=false).
   182: - name: Configure OVSDB managers on Open vSwitch nodes
   183:   hosts: network:compute
   184:   gather_facts: false
   185: 
   186:   vars:
   187:     northwatch_ovs_enabled: true
   188:     ovs_managers:
   189:       - "ptcp:6640:127.0.0.1"
   190:       - "ptcp:6640:{{ internal_address }}"
   191: 
   192:   tasks:
   193:     - name: Check whether the openvswitch_db container exists
   194:       become: true
   195:       ansible.builtin.command:
   196:         cmd: docker inspect openvswitch_db
   197:       register: ovs_db_container
   198:       changed_when: false
   199:       failed_when: false
   200:       when: northwatch_ovs_enabled | bool
   201: 
   202:     - name: Get currently configured OVSDB managers
   203:       become: true
   204:       ansible.builtin.command:
   205:         cmd: docker exec openvswitch_db ovs-vsctl get-manager
   206:       register: ovs_current_managers
   207:       changed_when: false
   208:       when:
   209:         - northwatch_ovs_enabled | bool
   210:         - ovs_db_container.rc | default(1) == 0
   211: 
   212:     - name: Set OVSDB managers (TCP listener on port 6640)
   213:       become: true
   214:       ansible.builtin.command:
   215:         cmd: "docker exec openvswitch_db ovs-vsctl set-manager {{ ovs_managers | join(' ') }}"
   216:       changed_when: true
   217:       when:
   218:         - northwatch_ovs_enabled | bool
   219:         - ovs_db_container.rc | default(1) == 0
   220:         - (ovs_current_managers.stdout_lines | default([]) | map('trim') | sort | list)
   221:           != (ovs_managers | sort | list)

review_question: Would an average-task-size cutoff be a useful additional signal that this artifact needs decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Gateway collector — OpenTelemetry-recommended "gateway pattern" implementation.
     3: # Called from setup.yml when `opentelemetry_gateway_enabled: true`, *before*
     4: # the helm task so the gateway collector spec AND its supporting resources
     5: # (htpasswd Secret + Ingress) are included in the chart values.
     6: #
     7: # All resources go through helm via:
     8: #   - `collectors.<gateway_name>` (the OpenTelemetryCollector CR + the
     9: #     operator-spawned Service/Deployment) → driven by
    10: #     `opentelemetry_collectors[<gateway_name>]`
    11: #   - `extraObjects[]` (Secret + Ingress) → driven by
    12: #     `opentelemetry_additional_config.extraObjects`
    13: #
    14: # That way helm owns the full lifecycle: a `helm upgrade` after disabling
    15: # the gateway tears everything down, and credential rotation is reflected
    16: # through a pod-annotation checksum so the operator triggers a rollout.
    17: 
    18: - name: "Compute gateway derived values"
    19:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    20:     _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}"
    21:     _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}-htpasswd"
    22:     _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled: "{{ (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | default('') | length) > 0 }}"
    23: 
    24: - name: "Build the gateway collector spec"
    25:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    26:     opentelemetry_collectors: >-
    27:       {{
    28:         (opentelemetry_collectors | default({}))
    29:         | combine({ opentelemetry_gateway_name: _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec }, recursive=True)
    30:       }}
    31:   vars:
    32:     _volumes: >-
    33:       {{
    34:         [{
    35:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    36:           'secret': {'secretName': _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name}
    37:         }]
    38:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    39:       }}
    40:     _volume_mounts: >-
    41:       {{
    42:         [{
    43:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    44:           'mountPath': '/etc/otel-auth',
    45:           'readOnly': true
    46:         }]
    47:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    48:       }}
    49:     # Credential rotation: the basicauth/server extension caches the
    50:     # htpasswd file at startup, so secret content changes only take effect
    51:     # when the pod restarts. Putting a checksum of the content in
    52:     # podAnnotations makes the operator roll the pod whenever the content
    53:     # differs from the previous apply.
    54:     _pod_annotations: >-
    55:       {{
    56:         {'checksum/htpasswd': (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | hash('sha256'))}
    57:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    58:       }}
    59:     _extensions: >-
    60:       {{
    61:         {'basicauth/server': {'htpasswd': {'file': '/etc/otel-auth/htpasswd'}}}
    62:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    63:       }}
    64:     _service_extensions: >-
    65:       {{
    66:         ['basicauth/server']
    67:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    68:       }}
    69:     # Auto-wire basicauth/server onto the OTLP HTTP receiver. We deep-merge
    70:     # so the user keeps full control of receiver options (compression,
    71:     # max_recv_msg_size, …).
    72:     _otlp_http_auth_overlay:
    73:       otlp:
    74:         protocols:
    75:           http:
    76:             auth:
    77:               authenticator: "basicauth/server"
    78:     _receivers: >-
    79:       {{
    80:         opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    81:         | combine(_otlp_http_auth_overlay, recursive=True)
    82:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled
    83:         else opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    84:       }}
    85:     # If the user did not provide explicit pipelines, route every receiver +
    86:     # processor + exporter into metrics & logs pipelines. Works for the
    87:     # common case of homogeneous OTLP exporters; override when you have
    88:     # signal-specific routing.
    89:     _default_pipelines:
    90:       metrics:
    91:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    92:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    93:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    94:       logs:
    95:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    96:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    97:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    98:     _pipelines: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines if (opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines | length > 0) else _default_pipelines }}"
    99:     _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec:
   100:       enabled: true
   101:       mode: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_mode }}"
   102:       replicas: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_replicas }}"
   103:       # Predictable service name (`<release>-<gateway_name>-collector`),
   104:       # otherwise the chart defaults to `<release>-collector` which
   105:       # collides with any other non-daemon collector. Required for the
   106:       # Ingress backend reference below.
   107:       fullnameOverride: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   108:       resources: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_resources }}"
   109:       volumes: "{{ _volumes }}"
   110:       volumeMounts: "{{ _volume_mounts }}"
   111:       podAnnotations: "{{ _pod_annotations }}"
   112:       config:
   113:         extensions: "{{ _extensions }}"
   114:         receivers: "{{ _receivers }}"
   115:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors }}"
   116:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters }}"
   117:         service:
   118:           extensions: "{{ _service_extensions }}"
   119:           pipelines: "{{ _pipelines }}"
   120: 
   121: - name: "Inject the gateway Secret + Ingress as chart extraObjects"
   122:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   123:     opentelemetry_additional_config: >-
   124:       {{
   125:         (opentelemetry_additional_config | default({}))
   126:         | combine({
   127:             'extraObjects': (
   128:               ((opentelemetry_additional_config | default({})).extraObjects | default([]))
   129:               + _gateway_extra_objects
   130:             )
   131:           })
   132:       }}
   133:   when: _gateway_extra_objects | length > 0
   134:   vars:
   135:     _htpasswd_secret_obj:
   136:       apiVersion: "v1"
   137:       kind: "Secret"
   138:       metadata:
   139:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name }}"
   140:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   141:       type: "Opaque"
   142:       stringData:
   143:         htpasswd: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd }}"
   144:     _ingress_obj:
   145:       apiVersion: "networking.k8s.io/v1"
   146:       kind: "Ingress"
   147:       metadata:
   148:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   149:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   150:         annotations: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_annotations }}"
   151:       spec:
   152:         ingressClassName: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_class_name }}"
   153:         tls: >-
   154:           {{
   155:             [{
   156:               'hosts': [opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname],
   157:               'secretName': opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_secret_name
   158:             }]
   159:             if opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_enabled else []
   160:           }}
   161:         rules:
   162:           - host: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname }}"
   163:             http:
   164:               paths:
   165:                 - path: "/"
   166:                   pathType: "Prefix"
   167:                   backend:
   168:                     service:
   169:                       name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}-collector"
   170:                       port:
   171:                         name: "otlp-http"
   172:     _gateway_extra_objects: >-
   173:       {{

    41: 
    42:     # Workspace personality files (issue #358). `force: no` means a
    43:     # subsequent `clawctl agent configure` run never clobbers user edits to
    44:     # these MD files — they seed the daemon on first configure, then the
    45:     # operator owns the content. BOOTSTRAP.md is intentionally NOT
    46:     # rendered: the runtime generates it on first boot and self-deletes
    47:     # after use.

    50:         path: "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/workspace"
    51:         state: directory
    52:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
    53:         group: "{{ agent_name }}"
    54:         mode: "0700"
    55: 
    56:     - name: Render zeroclaw workspace personality files

    58:         src: "{{ template_path }}/workspace/{{ item }}.j2"
    59:         dest: "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/workspace/{{ item }}"
    60:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
    61:         group: "{{ agent_name }}"
    62:         mode: "0600"
    63:         force: no

    65:         - SOUL.md
    66:         - IDENTITY.md
    67:         - USER.md
    68:         - AGENTS.md
    69:         - TOOLS.md
    70:         - MEMORY.md
    71:         - HEARTBEAT.md
    72: 
    73:     # Render ~/.zeroclaw/config.toml. no_log because provider_api_key is
    74:     # embedded verbatim. 0600 with agent ownership so only the service user
    75:     # (and root) can read. Ansible's default `force: yes` (not set here)
    76:     # only restarts the daemon when content changes — ATX S1 fix.
    77:     # #583: deploy the pre-rendered config.toml from
    78:     # `clawrium.core.render.render_zeroclaw` instead of re-rendering
    79:     # the same Jinja template under Ansible's environment. The
    80:     # canonical Python renderer owns the single source of truth for
    81:     # the file contents (including the custom `toq` filter); Ansible
    82:     # just lays the bytes down. This eliminates the dual-render hazard
    83:     # where the Python path and the Ansible path could silently
    84:     # diverge.
    85:     - name: Deploy ~/.zeroclaw/config.toml (pre-rendered canonical content)
    86:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    87:         content: "{{ prerendered_zeroclaw_config_toml }}"
    88:         dest: "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/config.toml"
    89:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
    90:         group: "{{ agent_name }}"
    91:         mode: "0600"
    92:       no_log: true
    93:       notify: Restart zeroclaw service
    94: 
    95:     # #851: slack-mcp-server install lives in the dedicated
    96:     # `install_slack_mcp.yaml` runbook invoked at sync time from
    97:     # `core.lifecycle_canonical._zeroclaw_install_slack_mcp`. This
    98:     # `configure.yaml` no longer installs the binary — the runbook
    99:     # pattern matches hermes (Phase 1) and openclaw (Phase 2) so a
   100:     # future pin bump propagates through one path instead of two.
   101: 
   102:     - name: Enable zeroclaw service
   103:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   104:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
   105:         enabled: yes
   106:         daemon_reload: yes
   107: 
   108:     # systemd drop-in directory (#422). Hosts the clawctl-managed Environment=
   109:     # overlay without touching the install.yaml-dropped unit file. Drop-ins
   110:     # are the systemd-standard mechanism per `man systemd.unit` "Drop-In".
   111:     - name: Ensure systemd drop-in directory exists for zeroclaw service
   112:       ansible.builtin.file:
   113:         path: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service.d"
   114:         state: directory
   115:         owner: root
   116:         group: root
   117:         mode: "0755"
   118: 
   119:     # Bundle 5 (#510) renamed the dropin from `10-clm-env.conf` to
   120:     # `10-zeroclaw-env.conf`. On a host that was last configured before
   121:     # the rename, the old file still exists in the dropin dir and systemd
   122:     # will load BOTH dropins — leaving stale GITHUB_TOKEN values readable
   123:     # under the old name. Drop the legacy file first so the dropin dir
   124:     # only ever contains the current managed file. Idempotent: state:
   125:     # absent is a no-op once the orphan is gone.
   126:     - name: Remove legacy clawctl dropin (Bundle 5 #510 rename migration)
   127:       ansible.builtin.file:
   128:         path: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service.d/10-clm-env.conf"
   129:         state: absent
   130:       no_log: true
   131:       notify: Restart zeroclaw service
   132: 
   133:     # Render the GitHub-integration drop-in. The template emits an empty
   134:     # [Service] block when no github integrations are assigned — systemd
   135:     # treats that as a no-op overlay. Mode 0600 because the file contains
   136:     # the GITHUB_TOKEN verbatim (read-only to root; systemd is started as
   137:     # root so this is fine). notify the restart handler so the drop-in is
   138:     # picked up before /health/providers is probed.
   139:     - name: Render zeroclaw GitHub-integration systemd drop-in
   140:       ansible.builtin.template:
   141:         src: "{{ template_path }}/zeroclaw-env.conf.j2"
   142:         dest: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service.d/10-zeroclaw-env.conf"
   143:         owner: root
   144:         group: root
   145:         mode: "0600"
   146:         force: yes
   147:       no_log: true
   148:       notify: Restart zeroclaw service
   149: 
   150:     # #649: github + git integration wiring moved to the canonical sync
   151:     # pipeline (`core/lifecycle_canonical.py:_setup_github_integration`).
   152:     # Fires on every `clawctl agent sync` when a `git` or `github`
   153:     # integration is attached, agent-type-agnostic. configure.yaml is
   154:     # not invoked by the modern kubectl-style CLI, so keeping the
   155:     # legacy `Render ~/.gitconfig` + `GitHub CLI authentication block`
   156:     # here was dead code — same class of bug as #755 / #834 (openclaw
   157:     # brave / hermes slack MCP install moved out of configure.yaml).
   158: 
   159:     # Apply pending restart (from the template task) before the readiness
   160:     # probe so /health is observing the just-rendered config, not the
   161:     # previous incarnation.
   162:     - name: Apply pending restart before probing
   163:       ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
   164: 
   165:     - name: Start zeroclaw service
   166:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   167:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
   168:         state: started
   169: 
   170:     # Fail fast if the daemon crashed on startup — better than waiting out
   171:     # 30×2s of /health retries (ATX W4). ActiveState may be `activating`
   172:     # momentarily; accept that as in-progress and let the health probe
   173:     # finish the wait.
   174:     - name: Verify zeroclaw service did not crash on startup
   175:       ansible.builtin.command:
   176:         cmd: "systemctl show -p ActiveState --value {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
   177:       register: service_state
   178:       changed_when: false
   179:       failed_when: service_state.stdout.strip() in ['failed', 'inactive']
   180: 
   181:     # Wait for the daemon to come up. /health/providers is the canonical
   182:     # readiness signal — it 200s only after the provider config has been
   183:     # parsed and the gateway is listening. Accept 401 too because the
   184:     # endpoint may require pairing-auth before serving — the existence of
   185:     # a response means the gateway is up.
   186:     - name: Probe /health/providers
   187:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   188:         url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/health/providers"
   189:         method: GET
   190:         status_code: [200, 401]
   191:         timeout: 5
   192:       register: health_probe
   193:       retries: 30
   194:       delay: 2
   195:       until: health_probe.status in [200, 401]
   196:       # ATX Round 3 S1: bring the health probe in line with the rest of
   197:       # the playbook's `no_log: true` hygiene. The probe body itself is
   198:       # non-secret but the registered `health_probe` is later used in
   199:       # `set_fact` branches gated on `status` — suppress to keep the
   200:       # log surface tight at high verbosity.
   201:       no_log: true
   202: 
   203:     # ATX Round 1 W3 + Round 2 W1 + Round 3 W1: surface a non-fatal
   204:     # warning when /health/providers returns 401. The gateway is up but
   205:     # the provider credentials probably mismatch the API key supplied in
   206:     # config.toml — chat calls will fail at request time.
   207:     #
   208:     # The fact (not just the debug task) is what configure_agent reads —
   209:     # `ansible_runner.run(quiet=True)` does not surface `runner_on_debug`
   210:     # events, so a pure `debug:` task would be silently swallowed at the
   211:     # CLI layer. Recording it as a cacheable fact ensures the warning
   212:     # propagates through the same fact-cache path the bearer token uses.
   213:     #
   214:     # Round 3 W1: assign the literal boolean unconditionally so a healthy
   215:     # run (status 200) clears any stale `true` left over from a prior
   216:     # 401 — `cacheable: true` would otherwise keep the previous value
   217:     # persisted in Ansible's fact cache and emit a phantom warning on
   218:     # every subsequent configure.
   219:     - name: Record provider-health warning state
   220:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   221:         zeroclaw_provider_health_warning: "{{ health_probe.status == 401 }}"
   222:         cacheable: true
   223: 
   224:     - name: Warn when /health/providers returned 401
   225:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   226:         msg: >-
   227:           /health/providers returned 401 — gateway is reachable but
   228:           provider credentials may be invalid. Verify the API key for
   229:           provider '{{ config.provider.type }}' and re-run
   230:           `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` if needed.
   231:       when: health_probe.status == 401
   232: 
   233:     # Always re-pair (issue #437). The daemon does not persist bearer
   234:     # state across restarts, so the only way to make hosts.json
   235:     # structurally agree with the daemon is to mint a fresh token on
   236:     # every configure run. The trade-off (in-flight `clawctl agent chat` sessions
   237:     # on other machines need to reconnect) is accepted in exchange for
   238:     # eliminating the silent divergence class entirely.
   239:     - name: Run zeroclaw pair handshake
   240:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/pair.yaml
   241: 
   242:     # Discord-config verification (#422). Confirms the bot token + an
   243:     # allowlist landed in config.toml when Discord is enabled. grep -q so
   244:     # we get a clean exit status without leaking the rendered key into logs.
   245:     # Uses dict.get() pattern (not attribute access) so undefined keys
   246:     # don't error under Ansible 2.20+'s strict Jinja mode.
   247:     - name: Verify config.toml contains bot_token when Discord enabled
   248:       ansible.builtin.command:
   249:         cmd: grep -qE '^bot_token\s*=' "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/config.toml"
   250:       register: discord_token_check
   251:       changed_when: false
   252:       failed_when: discord_token_check.rc != 0
   253:       no_log: true
   254:       when:
   255:         - config.channels is defined
   256:         - config.channels.discord is defined
   257:         - config.channels.discord.enabled | default(false)
   258: 
   259:     # Autonomy block always renders, so the grep is unconditional. This
   260:     # catches a Jinja regression that drops the block (which would silently
   261:     # disable shell_env_passthrough → tools lose GITHUB_TOKEN, _SECRET, etc.).
   262:     - name: Verify config.toml renders [autonomy] block with shell_env_passthrough
   263:       ansible.builtin.command:
   264:         cmd: grep -qE '^shell_env_passthrough\s*=' "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/config.toml"
   265:       register: autonomy_check
   266:       changed_when: false
   267:       failed_when: autonomy_check.rc != 0
   268: 
   269:     - name: Display configure success
   270:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   271:         msg: |
   272:           ZeroClaw agent '{{ agent_name }}' configured with provider
   273:           '{{ config.provider.type }}'.
   274:           Pairing: fresh token minted (issue #437 — every lifecycle op re-pairs).
   275:           Service: {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service (active)
   276: 
   277:   handlers:
   278:     # Single canonical restart handler. daemon_reload covers config-file
   279:     # changes that don't touch the unit, and the same restart fires once per
   280:     # configure regardless of how many notify directives match.
   281:     - name: Restart zeroclaw service
   282:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   283:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
   284:         state: restarted
   285:         enabled: yes
   286:         daemon_reload: yes
